summary: Bahrain admits GCC citizens freely, and offers visas on arrival and eVisas to a broad list of nationalities including the EU, US, UK and much of Asia and Latin America; everyone else needs a visit visa arranged through a sponsor in Bahrain via the NPRA before travel.

conditionalWaivers.text: Residents of other GCC states can generally apply for a Bahrain eVisa (or obtain a visa on arrival) regardless of nationality. Confirm eligibility on evisa.gov.bh.

fee.notes: Approximate, including processing. The exact amount and the longer multi-entry options are shown during the online application.
Approximate — payable by card or cash at Bahrain International Airport and the King Fahd Causeway.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Bahrain.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not checked at the border; standard travel medical coverage is recommended.

onwardTicket.text: Visa-on-arrival and eVisa visitors should hold an onward or return ticket and be able to show where they are staying.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show means of support — a bank card and a modest amount of cash suffice.

currencyLimits.text: Cash and negotiable instruments worth BHD 6,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared on arrival.

notes: Non-Muslim adults may bring in a limited duty-free alcohol allowance — unlike some Gulf neighbors, alcohol is legal in licensed venues.
Narcotics offenses carry severe penalties, and some prescription medicines need prior approval. Carry prescriptions for any medication.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere in Manama, from malls to taxis; a little cash helps in the traditional souq.

safety.text: Bahrain is generally safe with low crime. Sporadic demonstrations can occur in some villages — avoid them — and rules on drugs, public behavior and drink-driving are strict.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Bahrain Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March is pleasantly warm for the forts, souqs and the Formula 1 weekend; summer is extremely hot and humid.

idp.text: Bahrain is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Bahrain is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Bahrain yet.

tips.text: Arriving from Saudi Arabia over the King Fahd Causeway? Visas on arrival and eVisas are accepted at the causeway border post too, but expect long lines on Thursday and Friday evenings when weekend traffic peaks.
Alcohol is legal in licensed hotels, bars and restaurants, but there is zero tolerance for drink-driving and public drunkenness can lead to arrest.
During Ramadan, eating, drinking or smoking in public in daylight hours is an offense — hotels serve visitors discreetly, and many restaurants open only after sunset.
Hotel prices and flight loads spike around the Bahrain Grand Prix in spring. Book well ahead if your dates overlap the race weekend.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bahrain?
faq.answer: GCC citizens enter freely with a national ID. A broad list of nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia and much of Asia and Latin America — can get a visa on arrival or apply online for an eVisa. Nationalities outside those lists need a visit visa arranged through a sponsor in Bahrain (a hotel, company or relative) via the NPRA before travel.

faq.question: Should I get the Bahrain eVisa or a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: If you are eligible for both, the visa on arrival is quickest. It is issued at the airport or the King Fahd Causeway in minutes. The eVisa (evisa.gov.bh) is worth getting in advance if you prefer certainty before boarding, want a longer or multi-entry option, or are only eligible for the eVisa and not for the visa on arrival.

faq.question: I live in Saudi Arabia / the UAE — can I get a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Generally yes: residents of GCC states in valid residence status can obtain a Bahrain eVisa or visa on arrival regardless of nationality. Check your eligibility on evisa.gov.bh before traveling, as conditions attach to residence-permit validity and profession.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Bahrain?
faq.answer: Since the 2020 normalisation agreement Israeli passport holders have been able to obtain Bahraini visas, but the arrangement is sensitive to regional events and practical access has fluctuated. Verify the current position on evisa.gov.bh or with a Bahraini mission before booking.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bahrain?
faq.answer: Yes — visit visas can usually be extended through the NPRA before your current period expires, online or at its offices. Overstaying incurs a per-day fine, so apply in good time.
